_why: ORIENT2h6 (D151's ORIENT2h3, ORIENT2h4 and ORIENT2h6 notes; .claude/knowledge/twins.md): which lines of a markdown file a fenced code block holds, read as CommonMark reads a fence. A fence opens on a run of three or more backticks or tildes after any indent, and closes only on a run of the same character at least as long with nothing after it but spaces; a backtick run with a backtick later on its line is code inline and opens nothing; a fence never closed holds the rest of the file. One table its readers are held to, row for row: the CLI's markdownFence (src/document.ts, which firstHeading reads by) and the tools' fenced (tools/doc-duplicates.mjs) in test/markdown-fence.test.ts, and the driver's SelfDescription.Fence in SelfDescriptionTests. The service's MarkdownFence is held to the tools' fenced by tools/orient-index-fixtures/decision-notes.json. Each case: why, the file's lines, and the lines a fence holds, from 1, its opening and closing lines included.

cases.why: three backticks open a fence and three close it
a four-backtick fence quoting a three-backtick example closes only on four
a four-backtick fence quoting a frontmatter-shaped block and an underlined heading
a tilde fence opens, and a backtick run inside it closes nothing
a backtick fence, and a tilde run inside it closes nothing
a closing run longer than the opening one closes it
a closing run shorter than the opening one closes nothing
a run with text after it closes nothing, an info string included
spaces, a tab or a carriage return after a closing run still close it
a backtick run with a backtick later on its line is code inline and opens nothing
a tilde run may have backticks after it, and opens a fence
two backticks or two tildes open nothing
a run after text on its line opens nothing
a fence opens and closes after any indent, a tab's or four spaces' too
a second fence after the first, each of its own kind
a fence never closed holds the rest of the file, its last empty line too
